Insight: 1.2 billion tobacco users in 2024 (1 in 5 adults); the 2025 target of a 30% reduction was missed (27%). Europe has the highest prevalence (24.1%)
Needs or potential: Potential: very large global target group; Europe is a priority region

Insight: First global estimate of e-cigarette use: more than 100 million people vape
Needs or potential: Need: the app must handle dual use and vaping, not only cigarettes

Source: Special Eurobarometer on tobacco and nicotine (2024)
Insight: EU smoking prevalence ~24%; ~53% of smokers have ever tried to quit; dual users try more often (68%)
Needs or potential: Potential: about half of EU smokers have quit-attempt experience, so there is a large group in the volitional and recovery phases

Insight: Belgium: 12.8% daily smokers (15.4% in 2018); 39% of smokers plan to quit within a year; national target < 10% by 2028
Needs or potential: Need: 61% are not planning to quit soon, so the motivational-phase module matters

Reference: Jackson et al. (2025), JAMA Netw Open (PMC11742533; verify authors)
Insight: 40.8% of quit attempts were unaided; e-cigarettes were used in 40.2%; websites in 4.6% (and associated with success, OR 1.43)
Needs or potential: Potential: most attempts use no evidence-based help. Need: integrate e-cigarettes as a path

Insight: US$1.4 trillion per year (1.8% of world GDP); 5.7% of global health expenditure
Needs or potential: Potential: payers and employers have strong economic reasons to fund cessation

Source: Quit-smoking app market reports (GIR, Verified MR, Bosson, WiseGuy)
Reference: Market Publishers (2026); Verified Market Research; WiseGuy Reports
Insight: 2025 size estimates range from US$0.5 to 1.7 billion, with CAGR of 9–16%
Needs or potential: Potential: a growing niche; the numbers are uncertain

Insight: ~US$38 billion in 2026 (mostly NRT and medication). Digital apps and quitlines are small, but many insurance plans require them
Needs or potential: Potential: an app that drives medication uptake taps into the larger aids market

Source: UK discrete choice experiment, n = 337 smokers
Insight: WTP for app attributes: about +US$7 one-off for a 4.8-star rating, +US$2.6 for a trusted health organisation; the app description did not affect choice
Needs or potential: WTP: consumer WTP is low; uptake is driven by ratings and trust

Source: Smoke Free pricing and public purchasing
Reference: Smoke Free store listings; UK council notices (North Lincs, Lambeth)
Insight: Premium ~£60 (UK) or US$13–40/year; UK councils buy free premium access for residents
Needs or potential: WTP: B2G (public health) is a working channel for evidence-based apps

Insight: Two smoking apps are reimbursed (NichtraucherHelden, permanent since 2023; Smoke Free, listed). Average DiGA price ~€361 (2024)
Needs or potential: WTP: insurers pay hundreds of euros per user once clinical evidence exists

Insight: US$58M Series C (US$151M total); sold to employers and health plans; claims 3.0× ROI on medical claims (substance use overall)
Needs or potential: WTP: B2B employer market (mainly US) values cessation programmes with coaching and medication

Insight: Tabacologist consultations reimbursed since 2009; Tabakstop quitline free; mHealthBelgium M3 reimbursement exists but no smoking app reached it
Needs or potential: Potential (BE): partner with existing reimbursed care instead of selling the app

Source: Systematic review: smokers' user experience of cessation apps (28 studies)
Insight: Users want simplicity, personalisation, diverse content forms, interactivity, and privacy and security
Needs or potential: Need: direct support for personalisation, and for opt-in data with visible privacy controls

Source: Qualitative study, Black smokers (QuitGuide as reference)
Insight: Themes: content, format, functionality, social network, and inclusivity (culturally relevant information)
Needs or potential: Need: building blocks should allow culturally tailored content variants

Source: Qualitative study, young adults quitting e-cigarettes (n = 12)
Insight: Want flexible personalisation (set and change own goals), tracking, moderated anonymous peer support, positively framed notifications
Needs or potential: Need: user control over goals and notification tone; buddy/peer block as an option

Source: Objective engagement with health apps (panel data, 93 apps)
Insight: Median 15-day retention 3.9%, 30-day 3.3%
Needs or potential: Need: the first two weeks decide everything; the intake and early phase must deliver value fast

Insight: Most smokers are ambivalent about quitting; motivational support in apps is limited to money calculators
Needs or potential: Potential: an under-served segment where an MI chatbot fits

Reference: Research Live (EU vs US wearables); Statista/Ofcom UK (2025)
Insight: EU wearable ownership is about half of the US level; good EU-wide figures are scarce
Needs or potential: Need: wearable must stay optional; phone-only and EMA-only tiers carry most users

Reference: Review cited in QuitSure studies (2023; verify)
Insight: 88.5% of 104 cessation apps had not been updated in over a year
Needs or potential: Potential: the market is full of stale apps; a maintained, evidence-graded app stands out
